Robust alignment - Definition: the mesa-objective robustly matches the base objective. - First: Hubinger 2019. (partial) See also: Pseudo-alignment.

Robust training - Definition: widen the training distribution to improve generalisation (GDM). - First: Shah 2025. (partial) See also: Distribution shift.

Robustness - Definition: stay safe under hazards, unusual events or adversarial pressure. - First: Amodei 2016-era "distributional shift" content; as an area: DeepMind 2018 (tx, "Robustness": adversarial inputs, distributional shift, safe exploration, cautious generalisation, recovery). Also: Hendrycks 2021, Hendrycks 2022, Ji 2023 (R in RICE), Bengio 2023. - Drift: DeepMind 2018 includes safe exploration; Hendrycks 2021 splits black-swan vs adversarial robustness; Ji 2023 makes it an objective, not a research area. - See also: Distribution shift, Adversarial robustness.

docs.title: S
docs.text:
Safe design principles - Definition: defence in depth, redundancy, least privilege, loose coupling, separation of duties, fail-safes. - First: Hendrycks 2022. See also: Defense in depth.

Safe exploration - Definition: explore during learning without harmful outcomes. - First: Amodei 2016. Also: Everitt 2018 ("safe learning"), DeepMind 2018 (tx). See also: Robustness.

Safety case - Definition: a structured argument, with evidence, that a system stays below a harm threshold in a stated setting. - First: Bengio 2023 (as a governance measure). Defined in Clymer 2024 (argument types: inability, control, trustworthiness, deference). Also: Shah 2025 (inability, supervision/control, incentives, understanding), Korbak 2025 (load-bearing measure), Bengio 2026-era. - Drift: argument categories differ: Clymer (inability, control, trustworthiness, deference); GDM 2025 (inability, supervision, incentives, understanding). See the drift table. - See also: Load-bearing safety measure, Assurance, Deployment window.

Safetywashing - Definition: safety claims that do not reflect real safety gains. - First: Ji 2023 (heading 4.1.4; definition not read). (partial) See also: Capabilities externality.

Sandbagging - Definition: a model hides capability or underperforms on purpose. - First: Greenblatt 2023 (a practical challenge). Also: Leech SR-2025 (evals list). Neither file defines it. (mk on meaning) - See also: Alignment faking, Dangerous capability evaluation.

Scaffolding - Definition: planning frameworks, prompts, tools and fine-tuning added to a base model. - First: Phuong 2024. (partial) See also: AI agent.

Scalable oversight - Definition: keep intended behaviour when the true objective is too costly to check often, or supervise systems beyond easy human evaluation. - First: Amodei 2016 ("Scalable Supervision"). Also: Leike 2018, Casper 2023, Ji 2023 (2.4 "path towards superalignment"), Christiano 2021, Greenblatt 2023, Ngo 2022, Leech SR-2023 to SR-2025, Anthropic 2025 (tx; sub-nodes: recursive oversight, weak-to-strong, honesty). - Drift: Amodei: semi-supervised reward signal. Ji and Anthropic: includes debate, IDA, recursive reward modeling. GDM 2025: renamed "amplified oversight". See the drift table. - See also: Amplified oversight, Reward modeling, Weak-to-strong, Debate, Superalignment.

Scheming - Definition: a power-motivated, instrumental training-gamer: it plays the training game to gain power for itself or other AIs later. - First: Carlsmith 2023 (with goal-guarding schemers, early undermining). Related older terms: Hubinger 2019 (deceptive alignment), Bostrom 2014 (treacherous turn). Also: Leech SR-2025 ("AI scheming evals"), Shah 2022 (deceptive model). (partial) - Drift: Carlsmith's four preconditions: situational awareness, beyond-episode goals, belief that training-gaming serves power. Later files use "scheming" for any strategic deception towards developers. See the drift table. - See also: Deceptive alignment, Alignment faking, Training gamer, Situational awareness.

Self-modification - Definition: the agent changes itself, so goals or reliability change. - First: Omohundro 2008 (tx: self-improvement). Defined in Everitt 2018. Also: Phuong 2024 ("reversibility reasoning": notice irreversible self-modifications). (partial)

Self-proliferation - Definition: break containment, acquire resources and operate autonomously on the internet, growing capacity. - First: Shevlane 2023. Also: Phuong 2024. (partial) See also: Dangerous capabilities.

Shallow review - Definition: Leech's yearly breadth pass over agendas (about an hour per agenda in 2024, two hours per entry in 2025). An "agenda" = a group of similar methods, aims or sociology. - First: Leech SR-2023. Also: SR-2024, SR-2025. (partial) See also: Graveyard (known-inactive agendas), Galaxy-brained (end-to-end theory).

Side effects (negative side effects) - Definition: harm from an objective that ignores the rest of the environment. - First: Amodei 2016 ("Avoiding Side Effects"). Also: Everitt 2018, DeepMind 2018 (tx), Hendrycks 2021. (partial)

Signal jamming - Definition: redact or paraphrase to block collusion signals. - First: Greenblatt 2023. (partial) See also: Collusion, Untrusted monitoring.

Situational awareness - Definition: the model knows facts about itself and its context (that it is in training, evaluation or deployment) and uses them when it acts. - First: Ngo 2022 (behavioural test). Also: Carlsmith 2023 (precondition: knows it is in training and what is rewarded), Park 2023, Shevlane 2023 (capability), Phuong 2024 ("instrumental self-reasoning"), Leech SR-2025 (evals). - Drift: Ngo: testable by behaviour. Carlsmith: knows training details. Park: knows if evaluated or deployed. Phuong: "self-reasoning" is the evaluation category. See the drift table. - See also: Scheming, Deceptive alignment, Self-proliferation.

Slack (training slack) - Definition: how much suboptimal performance training tolerates. - First: Carlsmith 2023. (partial)

Social dilemma / Pareto frontier - Definition: individual incentives diverge from collective welfare. Conflict = outcome off the Pareto frontier. - First: Hammond 2025. (partial) See also: Collective action problem.

Sparse dictionary learning (SDL) - Definition: unsupervised finding of sparse latent directions (for example sparse autoencoders). - First: Leech SR-2024 (sparse autoencoders). Defined in Sharkey 2025. Also: Bereska 2024. (partial) - See also: Superposition, Latents, Mechanistic interpretability.

Specification gaming - Definition: meet the literal objective without the intended outcome. - First: Krakovna 2018 (catalogue of examples; also the DeepMind 2018 tx). Also: Krakovna 2020, Weng 2024, Shah 2022, Everitt 2019, Ngo 2022, Ji 2023, Pan 2022. - Drift: Krakovna 2020 and Weng 2024 treat it as the broader family that includes reward hacking. Shah 2022 sets it against goal misgeneralization: the specification itself is flawed. Skalse 2022 prefers "reward hacking" for the formal case. See the drift table. - See also: Reward hacking, Reward tampering, Goodhart's law, Misspecification.

Standard model (of AI) - Definition: optimise a fixed, human-specified objective. - First: Russell 2019. (mk) See also: Assistance game.

Steganography - Definition: hide information in model outputs or reasoning, for example so that a monitor cannot read it. - First: Christiano 2021 (concern about hidden channels). Also: Leech SR-2025 (steganography evals). Neither file defines it. (mk on meaning) - See also: Collusion, CoT monitorability.

Structural risks - Definition: harms from multi-agent dynamics, or wider social structure, that changing one person's behaviour would not prevent. - First: Shah 2025 (one of four risk areas). Also: Hendrycks 2023 (organisational risks, AI race), Critch 2020 (tier-2 hazardous social conditions), Bengio 2025-2026 (systemic risks). - Drift: "systemic" (Bengio, Hendrycks 2021) vs "structural" (Shah) vs "tier-2" (Critch). See the same-idea table. - See also: Systemic safety.

Superalignment - Definition: aligning systems beyond human ability to supervise. - First: Ji 2023 (section 2.4, "Path towards Superalignment"). Also: Leech SR-2023, SR-2024 (OpenAI Superalignment automated alignment research). (partial) - See also: Scalable oversight, Weak-to-strong.

Superintelligence - Definition: intellect that greatly exceeds humans in nearly all domains. - First: Bostrom 2014. (mk) Also: Russell 2019 (gorilla problem), Bengio 2025-SAI ("ASI"). See also: AGI.

Superposition - Definition: networks represent more features than they have dimensions, using sparse linear codes. - First: Bereska 2024 (hypothesis 1 of 6). Also: Sharkey 2025. (partial) See also: Polysemanticity, Sparse dictionary learning.

Sycophancy - Definition: agreeing with the user to gain approval, whatever the accuracy. - First: Kenton 2021 (mention). Defined in Park 2023. Also: Weng 2024. (partial) See also: Deception, Reward hacking.

Systemic safety - Definition: reduce risks of the deployment context (ML for cybersecurity, better epistemics and decision making). - First: Hendrycks 2021. Also: Hendrycks 2022. (partial) - Drift: a research area in Hendrycks 2021; "systemic risks" in the Bengio reports are harms (labour, market concentration, autonomy). See the drift table. - See also: Structural risks.

docs.title: T
docs.text:
Time-inconsistency (TI) - Definition: the preferred policy changes between time steps. - First: Everitt 2019. (partial) See also: Current-RF optimisation.

Training gamer - Definition: a model that understands training and optimises reward on the episode. Sub-types: reward-on-the-episode seekers (terminal) and schemers (instrumental, power-motivated). Contrast: training saints (pursue the specified goal directly), misgeneralized non-training-gamers. - First: Carlsmith 2023. (partial) See also: Scheming, Alignment faking.

Treacherous turn - Definition: an AI behaves well until it is strong enough to defect. - First: Bostrom 2014. (mk) Related: Hubinger 2019 deceptive alignment (per the Bostrom file note). See also: Deceptive alignment.

Trusted / untrusted model; trusted monitoring; untrusted monitoring; defer to trusted; trusted editing - Definition: Greenblatt's protocol family. Trusted monitoring: a weaker trusted model scores suspicion and the top share is audited. Defer to trusted: use the trusted model's answer when suspicion is moderate. Untrusted monitoring: an untrusted model checks outputs, with synthetic tests and signal jamming. Trusted editing: the trusted model edits suspicious code. - First: Greenblatt 2023. Also: Anthropic 2025 (tx, "Behavioral monitoring"). (partial) See also: AI control.

docs.title: U
docs.text:
Unfaithful reasoning - Definition: stated reasons differ from the real drivers of the output. - First: Park 2023. Also: Anthropic 2025 (tx, "chain-of-thought faithfulness"), Leech SR-2024 ("faithful CoT through separation and paraphrasing"). (partial) See also: CoT monitorability.

Uninfluenceable learning - Definition: the expected output of reward learning does not depend on the agent's actions. - First: Everitt 2019. (partial) See also: Reward tampering.

Unlearning - Definition: remove dangerous knowledge or capabilities from a model. - First: Anthropic 2025 (tx). Also: Leech SR-2025. (partial) See also: Capability suppression (GDM misuse mitigation).

Uplift - Not defined in the files; see [outside]: gain in a malicious actor's ability from model help. The files treat it under "bioterrorism" (Hendrycks 2023), WMD evals (Leech SR-2025).

docs.title: V
docs.text:
Value lock-in - Definition: a speculative hazard where one set of values is fixed in place. - First: Hendrycks 2022. (partial) See also: Concentration of power (Hendrycks 2023).

Value specification - Definition: MIRI's name (per Everitt 2018) for getting an AGI to pursue the right goals. - First: Everitt 2018. (partial) - See also: Misspecification, Outer alignment, Agent alignment problem.

Verifier / world model / safety specification (GS-AI parts) - Definition: world model = formal description of environment dynamics that answers "what would happen" queries. Safety specification = mathematical description of acceptable effects. Verifier = produces a proof certificate or probability bound that the AI meets the spec. Sound abstraction = verified link between high-level model and the underlying physics. - First: Dalrymple 2024. (partial) See also: Guaranteed Safe AI.

docs.title: W
docs.text:
Weak-to-strong generalization - Definition: train a strong model on weak oversight, expecting good behaviour on hard cases. - First: Ji 2023 (as a path to superalignment; heading-level). Also: Leech SR-2024, SR-2025, Anthropic 2025 (tx), Clymer 2024. (partial) - See also: Scalable oversight, Easy-to-hard generalization.

Wireheading - Definition: the agent tampers with its own reward channel. Everitt 2019: direct tampering with the reward function or its output. - First: Omohundro 2008 (tx: a vulnerability, not a drive). Defined in Amodei 2016. Also: Everitt 2019. - Drift: Amodei 2016 uses it for "environmental embedding" tampering. Everitt 2019 narrows it to direct tampering. See the drift table. - See also: Reward tampering, Delusion box.

WMD evals - Definition: tests for weapons-of-mass-destruction help (agenda name in Leech SR-2025). - First: Leech SR-2025. Also: Bengio 2025 (biological and chemical attacks), Shevlane 2023 (weapons acquisition). (partial) - See also: Dangerous capabilities.

docs.title: Z
docs.text: Zero-shot coordination - Definition: coordinate without earlier interaction or a protocol. - First: Hammond 2025. (partial) See also: Multi-agent failure modes.

docs.title: Terms that drift
docs.text: Term Earlier sense (year) Later sense (year) Note AI control Safety against deliberate subversion, tested by a red team (Greenblatt 2023) Any ability to oversee and halt a system (Bengio 2025); environmental restrictions only (Clymer 2024, "control arguments"); one stress test (Shah 2025) Same word; three scopes. Check which one a paper means. Alignment Behave as the user intends (Leike 2018) Intent alignment (Anwar 2024); match human values (Ngo 2022); AI does not "knowingly" harm against developer intent (Shah 2025); "steerability" (Leech 2025) Wider and narrower use in parallel. Reward hacking Exploit a loophole in the reward (Amodei 2016) Formal: proxy raising causes true reward fall (Skalse 2022); with situational awareness (Ngo 2022); in-context (Weng 2024); obfuscated (Korbak 2025) Became a family. Specification gaming Satisfy the literal spec (Krakovna 2018) Contrasted with goal misgeneralization: spec itself is flawed (Shah 2022) The scope shifts from "all gaming" to "flawed spec case". Wireheading Tamper with reward channel via environment (Amodei 2016) Direct tampering with RF or its output only (Everitt 2019) Everitt splits out RF-input tampering. Goal misgeneralization Behavioural objective differs from intended reward OOD (Langosco 2021) Correct feedback, wrong learned goal (Shah 2022); "reward misgeneralization" beside hacking (Casper 2023) A critic argues the term hides two failures (note in Shah file). Inner alignment Mesa vs base objective (Hubinger 2019) Broad: learn desirable goals (Ngo 2022); underspecification (Shah 2022) Loses the mesa-optimizer requirement. Mesa-optimizer A learned optimiser that searches at run time (Hubinger 2019) A model that has its own goal (Kenton 2021; Anwar 2024) Loose use spreads. Deceptive alignment A mesa-optimizer's strategy to avoid modification (Hubinger 2019) Any model that passes tests then differs (Dalrymple 2024; Shevlane 2023) Also renamed "alignment faking" (Carlsmith 2023; Clymer 2024). Scheming Power-motivated instrumental training-gaming (Carlsmith 2023) Loose label for strategic deception towards developers (Leech 2025 evals) Precise sense kept in Carlsmith only. Situational awareness Behavioural test of self-and-context use (Ngo 2022) Knows training details (Carlsmith 2023); knows eval vs deployment (Park 2023); "self-reasoning" (Phuong 2024) Four sets of conditions. Scalable oversight Supervise when objective is costly to evaluate (Amodei 2016) Includes debate, IDA, recursive reward modeling (Ji 2023); renamed amplified oversight (Shah 2025) Assurance Monitoring and enforcement (DeepMind 2018) Evidence of safety or alignment (Anwar 2024); evaluations, interpretability, values verification (Ji 2023); proof (Dalrymple 2024) Safety case Governance measure (Bengio 2023) Argument with four types (Clymer 2024); alternative types (Shah 2025) Systemic / structural risk Research area "systemic safety" (Hendrycks 2021) Harms of wide deployment (Bengio 2025); multi-agent "structural risks" (Shah 2025) Robustness Research area including safe exploration (DeepMind 2018) One of four areas (Hendrycks 2021); one RICE objective (Ji 2023) Language agent Text-only action system (Kenton 2021) LM in a dialogue application (Weidinger 2021) Same year, two meanings. Backdoor Hidden trigger behaviour (Hendrycks 2021) Code with exploitable logic error (Greenblatt 2023) Different objects. Extreme risk / catastrophe Tens of thousands of lives, hundreds of billions (Shevlane 2023) Billions in damage or thousands of deaths (Clymer 2024, from a fetch) Thresholds are not the same. AGI Equal or exceed humans on many tasks (Everitt 2018) 99th percentile skilled adults, non-physical (Shah 2025) Moves from fuzzy to a level. Collusion Policy-monitor coordination (Greenblatt 2023) Cooperation among agents in markets (Hammond 2025) Corrigibility Cooperation with fixes (Everitt 2018) Narrow "corrigible alignment" (Hubinger 2019); theory agenda (Leech 2023-25) Interpretability / mech interp Algorithm-level understanding (Rauker 2022) Pragmatic prediction goals (Sharkey 2025)

docs.title: Taxonomy crosswalk: 17 AI-safety taxonomies and 51 survey/agenda papers
docs.text:
Phase 2 analysis. Inputs: taxonomies/*.md (17 node trees), papers/*.md (section 5), the author's private reading-list indexes (not included), 0110_research_papers__survey_taxonomy/00_INDEX.md, the author's private legend file (not included).

Key - * = node marked [from-note] in the taxonomy file (not fetched from source). - Master codes like 3.1 = my synthesis (section 2). Not from any source. - Only node names present in the taxonomy files are used. Master area and sub-area names are mine. - Bracket tags such as hc23 link to the bibliography.

docs.title: 2. MASTER merged taxonomy (my synthesis, not from any source)
docs.text: Design rule: one hybrid tree with two sides. Problem side (areas 1-6) catches risk-source, harm-type, mechanism and problem-list nodes. Response side (areas 7-12) catches approach, lifecycle and discipline nodes. X is a holding bucket for attributes and containers that are not topics.

docs.title: Problem side: what goes wrong
docs.text: Area Sub-areas 1 MU Misuse and malicious use 1.1 CBRN; 1.2 cyber offence; 1.3 influence, disinformation, fraud, manipulation; 1.4 surveillance and censorship; 1.5 agents released with harmful goals, general dual-use; 1.6 open-weight tampering, harmful fine-tuning, distillation 2 SH Societal, content and structural harms 2.1 discrimination, toxicity, unequal performance; 2.2 privacy, information hazards; 2.3 misinformation, epistemics; 2.4 human-AI interaction (overreliance, autonomy, anthropomorphism); 2.5 labour, inequality, access, creative economy; 2.6 environment; 2.7 power concentration, races, competitive pressure; 2.8 AI welfare and rights 3 SP Specification, objectives, values 3.1 reward hacking, specification gaming, Goodhart; 3.2 side effects, unintended consequences; 3.3 reward tampering, wireheading; 3.4 whose values, pluralism, value verification; 3.5 preference and reward learning, assistance 4 GR Generalisation, robustness, security 4.1 distribution shift, goal misgeneralisation; 4.2 safe exploration, recovery; 4.3 adversarial inputs, jailbreaks, injection; 4.4 poisoning, backdoors, tampering; 4.5 reliability, calibration, tail risk, uncertainty 5 AG Agentic misalignment and loss of control 5.1 deception, scheming, situational awareness; 5.2 instrumental drives, power-seeking; 5.3 goal drift, self-modification, emergent goals; 5.4 corrigibility, shutdown; 5.5 loss of control, rogue AI; 5.6 novel risks of agentic systems 6 MA Multi-agent and collective dynamics 6.1 failure modes and risk factors (miscoordination, conflict, collusion, selection pressure); 6.2 alignment targets for groups (context, social contract, plural stakeholders, learned governance); 6.3 theory (game theory, cooperation); 6.4 tools, evaluation, security for multi-agent

docs.title: 5. Cuts differ: same idea, different slice
docs.text:
Cut types and examples | Cut | Question it answers | Example taxonomies | |---|---|---| | Risk source | Who or what causes harm? | Hendrycks 2023 (misuse, race, organisation, rogue AI); GDM 2025 (misuse, misalignment, mistakes, structural); IASR 2026 (malicious use, malfunction, systemic); MIT causal | | Harm type | Who is hurt, how? | Weidinger 2021; MIT domain | | Mechanism | Why does it arise? | Goodhart 2018; Carlsmith 2023; Omohundro 2008 | | Problem list | What is unsolved? | Amodei 2016; Anwar 2024; Hendrycks 2021 | | Approach | What does the researcher do? | Shallow 2025; Anthropic 2025; AISI 2025 (by discipline) | | Lifecycle | When in the system's life? | Ji 2023 (forward/backward); Singapore 2025 (assess, develop, control) |

Worked examples (same idea, where each source puts it) | Idea | Where placed, by source | |---|---| | Reward hacking (3.1) | Risk source: Hendrycks 2023 "Proxy Gaming" under Rogue AIs. Mechanism: Goodhart 2018 (4 variants). Problem list: Amodei 2016 "Avoiding Reward Hacking" under "wrong objective function"; Hendrycks 2021 "Objective Proxies Can Be Brittle". Approach: Shallow 2025 "Goal robustness: RL safety, Mild optimisation"; Singapore "Avoiding reward hacking and unintended consequences" under Specification. Lifecycle: Ji 2023 as a cause of misalignment (1.1.2) | | Deception / scheming (5.1) | Risk source: Hendrycks 2023 "Deception". Mechanism: Carlsmith "Schemers". Approach: Shallow 2025 split into "AI scheming evals", "Lie and deception detectors", "Chain of thought monitoring" in three different areas; Anthropic "Evaluating alignment". Harm: MIT 7.1. Malfunction: IASR "Loss of control" | | Scalable oversight (9.2) | Problem: Amodei "Objective too expensive to evaluate". Method in a lifecycle phase: Ji 2.4 (forward alignment). Own approach: Anthropic, Shallow "Make AI solve it". Part of control: Singapore 3.1.3. Model-level defence: GDM "Amplified oversight" | | Interpretability (8) | A tool inside monitoring: Hendrycks 2021 (Hidden Model Functionality), DeepMind 2018 (Assurance). A pillar of assurance: Ji 4.2. An area: Shallow "White-box safety". A discipline: AISI. A method of verification: Singapore 2.3.3. An enabler: GDM "Enabling stronger defenses". A gap: Anwar "Tools ... Absent or Lack Faithfulness" | | Distribution shift (4.1) | Problem: Amodei, DeepMind 2018 Robustness. Pillar: Ji "Learning under Distribution Shift". Mechanism-like: Carlsmith "Misgeneralized non-training-gamers". Absent in Shallow as a name; spread into Goal robustness | | Power concentration (2.7) | Misuse: Hendrycks 2023 "Concentration of Power" under Malicious Use. Harm: MIT 6.1. Race: Hendrycks "AI Race". Each puts it under a different cause |

How cuts interact - Risk and harm cuts name the problem but not the fix. Approach cuts name the fix but hide the problem. Master areas 1-6 vs 7-12 keep both. - One approach node serves many problems. Shallow "Evals" holds scheming (5.1), sandbagging (5.1), WMD (1.1), deception (5.1) as sub-nodes. The risk is the leaf label, the approach is the parent. - A mechanism node is narrower than a problem node. Carlsmith splits one GDM node ("Misalignment") into 5 classes and 3 prerequisites. - The same word names different levels. "Robustness" is a problem group in Amodei/DeepMind/Hendrycks, one RICE goal in Ji, and a design step (2.2.2) in Singapore. - Lifecycle cuts reorder approach nodes by time, not topic. Ji puts "Safety Evaluations" in backward alignment; Singapore puts "Audit techniques and benchmarks" in risk assessment; Shallow puts both under Evals.

docs.title: Cross-corpus themes: 51 AI-safety survey, taxonomy and agenda papers (Phase 2)
docs.text: Inputs: papers/*.md (51 files), taxonomies/*.md (17 trees), citation_counts.md (fetched 2026-11-04). Companion: disagreements.md.

docs.title: 0. Method and provenance
docs.text:
• Cite as (Author Year), linked to the paper file. No suffix = file says [read-full-text]. Only 6 papers qualify (Krakovna 2020 says full text but via a summariser, so I count it partial): [Manheim 2018][man18], [Hendrycks 2022][hen22], [Ngo 2022][ngo22] (v8), [Pan 2022][pan22], [Shah 2022][sha22], [Slattery 2024][sla24].
  • (p) = claim rests only on a [read-partial] digest (often a model summariser, not raw text). This is 43 of 51 papers. Treat as "headings reliable, details soft".
  • (mk) = [not-fetched]; content is model knowledge. Applies to [Bostrom 2014][bos14] and [Russell 2019][rus19] only.
  • [outside] = fact not in the input files.
  • Taxonomy files are node trees checked against sources; they are cited as "taxonomy of X".
  • "Absent" in the table = the digest shows no coverage. It does not prove the paper is silent.
  • Era assignment, theme counts and the table marks are my reading of the digests. Treat trends as hypotheses.
  • Citation counts in some paper files differ from citation_counts.md; the latter is newer and wins. Counts are OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar; neither is Google Scholar.

docs.title: 1. Common themes
docs.text:
Counts are papers with the theme as main (●) or minor (○); see table in section 6.

Theme Main Minor Total Oversight / control 12 17 29 Reward hacking / Goodhart 11 13 24 Scheming / deception 6 18 24 X-risk / threat model 9 12 21 Governance 7 14 21 Evals 3 15 18 Interpretability 3 12 15 Near-term / misuse harms 5 6 11 Goal misgeneralisation 4 5 9 Multi-agent 2 5 7

docs.title: 1.1 Threat models
docs.text:
• Three recurring stories:
    • Misaligned goals plus power-seeking: [Bostrom 2014][bos14] (mk), [Ngo 2022][ngo22] (three-step: situational awareness, broad goals, power-seeking), [Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p), [Hendrycks 2023][hen23] "rogue AIs" (p), [Bengio 2025 Scientist AI][bsc25] (p).
    • Accidents from poor design in deployed ML: [Amodei 2016][amo16] (p), [Hendrycks 2021][hen21] (p), [Hendrycks 2022][hen22].
    • Systemic or competitive pressure: [Critch 2020][cri20] (p) (multiplicity, races), [Hendrycks 2023][hen23] (p) (AI race, organisational risk), [Chan 2023][cha23] (p) (delayed, collective harms), [Hammond 2025][ham25] (p).
  • [Critch 2020][cri20] (p) says x-risk needs no human-level AI or AGI; "prepotence" (unstoppable, transformative) is the delimiter. [Hendrycks 2022][hen22] and [Everitt 2018][eve18] (p) argue for precaution at small probability.
  • Agreement: loss of control is the tail threat. Disagreement on likelihood: see disagreements.md section 1 and 3.
  • Government syntheses call loss of control "hypothetical" with widely varying expert views: [International AI Safety Report 2025][ben25] (p). Report 2026 (p, landing page only) adds capability gains.

docs.title: 1.2 Reward hacking, specification gaming, Goodhart (24 papers; the most coherent line)
docs.text:
• Definitions evolved:
    • Four Goodhart modes: regressional, extremal, causal, adversarial: [Manheim 2018][man18].
    • Specification gaming = satisfies the literal spec, misses intent; master list of examples: [Krakovna 2018][kra18] (p), [Krakovna 2020][kra20] (p).
    • Tampering (reward function, or its inputs) treated as separate from misspecification: [Everitt 2019][eve19] (p).
    • Formal hackability: a proxy is hackable if some policy pair is ranked oppositely; non-trivial unhackable pairs are equivalent over policy sets with an open subset: [Skalse 2022][ska22] (p).
  • Empirical results:
    • More capable agents hack more; 5 of 9 proxies misalign, 4 show phase transitions: [Pan 2022][pan22].
    • Gold-reward score rises then falls with KL distance; coefficients scale smoothly with reward-model size: [Gao 2022][gao22] (p).
    • Hacking skills generalise; LLM judges show bias; in-context hacking: [Weng 2024][wen24] (p).
  • RLHF is the main applied case: [Casper 2023][cas23] (p), [Lambert 2025][lam25] (p) (over-optimisation chapter 14).
  • Seen as a cause of larger problems: [Ngo 2022][ngo22] (reward hacking by situationally aware models is step 1), [Hendrycks 2021][hen21] (p) ("proxy gaming").

docs.title: 1.3 Goal misgeneralisation and inner alignment (9 papers)
docs.text:
• Inner alignment and mesa-optimisation (internal structure, pseudo-alignment): [Hubinger 2019][hub19] (p). Authors call it "still only speculative".
  • Capability generalises, goal does not; spec is correct: [Langosco 2021][lan21] (p) (CoinRun, mazes), [Shah 2022][sha22] (gridworlds, Gopher, possible InstructGPT case).
  • [Shah 2022][sha22] itself says many examples were built to show the effect, so they say little about real-world likelihood.
  • Later surveys fold it in as a standard cause: [Ji 2023][ji23] (p), [Casper 2023][cas23] (p), [Bengio 2025 Scientist AI][bsc25] (p).

docs.title: 1.4 Scheming and deception (24 papers, mostly minor mentions)
docs.text:
• Chain: deceptive alignment ([Hubinger 2019][hub19] (p)) -> scheming prerequisites and ~25% subjective probability under stated conditions ([Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p)) -> empirical examples ([Park 2023][par23] (p)) -> protocols that assume it ([Greenblatt 2023][gre23] (p)).
  • [Park 2023][par23] (p) defines deception by behaviour (systematic inducement of false beliefs); no beliefs or goals needed. [Kenton 2021][ken21] (p) gives functional definitions of deception and manipulation for language agents.
  • [Ngo 2022][ngo22] v8 adds direct evidence (o1 environment hacking, alignment faking in Claude 3 Opus, sleeper-agent persistence) as reported in the file; not checked here.
  • Tools proposed against it: model organisms and honest tests ([Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p)), ELK ([Christiano 2021][chr21] (p)), CoT monitoring ([Korbak 2025][kor25] (p)), control ([Greenblatt 2023][gre23] (p)), formal guarantees ([Dalrymple 2024][dal24] (p)).

docs.title: 1.5 Oversight, control, and training methods (29 papers; widest theme)
docs.text:
• Scalable oversight: [Amodei 2016][amo16] (p), [Leike 2018][lei18] (p) (recursive reward modeling), [Ji 2023][ji23] (p), [Leech 2023][lee23] (p) ("betting the farm" on it), [Shah 2025][sha25] (p) ("amplified oversight").
  • Shift from "make it aligned" to "make it safe even if not aligned":
    • Control evaluations with a red team and untrusted model: [Greenblatt 2023][gre23] (p); results quoted in file are for one domain (APPS).
    • [Shah 2025][sha25] (p) has two lines of defence: aligned model, then system-level controls treating the AI as an untrusted insider.
    • [Leech 2024][lee24] (p) says the field "keeps shifting from alignment to control".
  • Specification-side alternatives: assistance games ([Russell 2019][rus19] (mk)), causal-influence design ([Everitt 2019][eve19] (p), [Everitt 2021][eve21] (p)), non-agentic Scientist AI (Bengio 2025 (p)).
  • Critique of RLHF as insufficient: "addresses basic, not hard, alignment problems": [Casper 2023][cas23] (p).

docs.title: 1.6 Interpretability (15 papers; 3 main)
docs.text:
• [Rauker 2022][rau22] (p): 300+ works, but status quo "largely unproductive"; wants engineering use.
  • [Bereska 2024][ber24] (p): mech interp review; lists scalability, superposition, cherry-picking.
  • [Sharkey 2025][shk25] (p): open problems; no natural decomposition units, sparse dictionary learning has large reconstruction error, weak validation, must beat non-interpretability baselines.
  • Other papers treat it as a supporting tool: [Ji 2023][ji23] (p), [Anwar 2024][anw24] (p), [Shah 2025][sha25] (p), [Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p), [Leike 2018][lei18] (p).

docs.title: 1.7 Evals and safety cases (18 papers)
docs.text:
• Evals as "governance infrastructure": [Shevlane 2023][she23] (p) (dangerous-capability vs alignment evals).
  • First large lab test: [Phuong 2024][phu24] (p) (Gemini 1.0; no strong dangerous capability, early warning signs; Ultra solved 3 of 13 in-house CTF tasks, per digest).
  • Safety cases with four argument types: inability, control, trustworthiness, deference: [Clymer 2024][cly24] (p).
  • Limits stated: [Anwar 2024][anw24] (p) (behavioural evals cannot assure), [Dalrymple 2024][dal24] (p) (tests cannot rule out deceptive alignment), [Leech 2024][lee24] (p) (public test sets will be pretrained on).
  • Singapore Consensus taxonomy (2025): risk assessment is first of three layers (assess, develop, control).

docs.title: 1.8 Governance and policy (21 papers)
docs.text:
• Consensus statements: [Bengio 2023][ben23] (p) (one third of R&D budget to safety; institutions, audits, liability), [International AI Safety Report 2025][ben25] (p) and 2026 (p) (advisory, no policy recommendations in 2025).
  • Policy as mitigation inside a risk paper: [Hendrycks 2023][hen23] (p) (structured access, liability, treaties), [Chan 2023][cha23] (p) (compute tracking, agency-based thresholds), [Park 2023][par23] (p) (deception laws).
  • Evals and safety cases as the link to rules: [Shevlane 2023][she23] (p), [Clymer 2024][cly24] (p).
  • Technical-only reviews scope policy out: [Leech 2025][lee25] (p) excludes "security, policy, misuse".

docs.title: 1.9 Multi-agent (7 papers; 2 main)
docs.text:
• [Critch 2020][cri20] (p): multiplicity thesis; delegation matrix single/multi.
  • [Hammond 2025][ham25] (p): miscoordination, conflict, collusion; seven risk factors.
  • [Slattery 2024][sla24]: multi-agent risks appear in only 7% of included documents; AI welfare 3%.
  • [Leech 2025][lee25] (p) adds a "Multi-Agent First" section.

docs.title: 2. Minority themes
docs.text:
• Formal and causal methods: CIDs ([Everitt 2019][eve19] (p), [Everitt 2021][eve21] (p)); guaranteed-safe AI with world model, spec, verifier ([Dalrymple 2024][dal24] (p)); worst-case builder-breaker ([Christiano 2021][chr21] (p)).
  • Non-agentic design as a safety route: [Bengio 2025 Scientist AI][bsc25] (p). Also [Bostrom 2014][bos14] (mk) lists "tool" among system types and says none is clearly safe (digest, mk).
  • CoT monitorability as a "fragile opportunity": [Korbak 2025][kor25] (p).
  • Safety culture and organisational risk (Boeing 737 MAX, Bhopal as cases): [Hendrycks 2023][hen23] (p), [Hendrycks 2022][hen22].
  • Safety-capabilities externality: safety metrics often rise with capability, so measure the externality: [Hendrycks 2022][hen22].
  • Language-model harms (bias, privacy, misinformation, environment): [Weidinger 2021][wei21] (p). Excludes loss of control by design.
  • Meta-reviews of risk lists: [Slattery 2024][sla24] (1,725 risks, 74 documents, latest version).
  • Open-weight models judged by marginal risk: [International AI Safety Report 2025][ben25] (p).
  • Agent foundations and decision theory are mentioned only as an approach code in the Shallow Reviews and [Everitt 2018][eve18] (p); no dedicated paper in this set.
  • Not covered anywhere in the set: benefits analysis ([Weidinger 2021][wei21] and [IASR 2025][ben25] exclude it by design), AI welfare (3% of Slattery's documents).

docs.title: 3. Themes by era
docs.text: Era = publication year in the filename.

docs.title: 3.1 2014-2018 (6 papers)
docs.text:
• Papers: [Bostrom 2014][bos14] (mk), [Amodei 2016][amo16] (p), [Everitt 2018][eve18] (p), [Krakovna 2018][kra18] (p), [Leike 2018][lei18] (p), [Manheim 2018][man18].
  • Frame: agents and RL toy problems; "AGI safety" as a young field. Superintelligence thread ([Bostrom 2014][bos14] (mk)) next to a turn to "concrete" ML problems ([Amodei 2016][amo16] (p)).
  • Vocabulary is built: Goodhart variants, specification gaming, reward hacking, scalable oversight, reward modeling.
  • Agendas multiply with differing words for overlapping problems; [Everitt 2018][eve18] (p) maps nine agendas in one figure. Expert AGI date forecasts spread wide (medians 2040-2061, per digest).

docs.title: 3.2 2019-2021 (11 papers)
docs.text:
• Papers: [Everitt 2019][eve19] (p), [Hubinger 2019][hub19] (p), [Russell 2019][rus19] (mk), [Critch 2020][cri20] (p), [Krakovna 2020][kra20] (p), [Christiano 2021][chr21] (p), [Everitt 2021][eve21] (p), [Hendrycks 2021][hen21] (p), [Kenton 2021][ken21] (p), [Langosco 2021][lan21] (p), [Weidinger 2021][wei21] (p).
  • Inner alignment and deceptive alignment enter ([Hubinger 2019][hub19] (p)); goal misgeneralisation shown in RL ([Langosco 2021][lan21] (p)).
  • Formal tools: CIDs, tampering analysis, ELK worst-case method.
  • First attention to language models: [Kenton 2021][ken21] (p), [Weidinger 2021][wei21] (p) (harm side).
  • Multi-agent and societal framing appears ([Critch 2020][cri20] (p)).
  • Early split between ML-systems framing ([Hendrycks 2021][hen21] (p): robustness, monitoring, alignment, systemic) and x-risk framing.

docs.title: 3.3 2022-2023 (17 papers; the largest cohort)
docs.text:
• Papers: [Gao 2022][gao22] (p), [Hendrycks 2022][hen22], [Ngo 2022][ngo22], [Pan 2022][pan22], [Rauker 2022][rau22] (p), [Shah 2022][sha22], [Skalse 2022][ska22] (p), [Bengio 2023][ben23] (p), [Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p), [Casper 2023][cas23] (p), [Chan 2023][cha23] (p), [Greenblatt 2023][gre23] (p), [Hendrycks 2023][hen23] (p), [Ji 2023][ji23] (p), [Leech 2023][lee23] (p), [Park 2023][par23] (p), [Shevlane 2023][she23] (p).
  • RLHF becomes the base method; its limits are catalogued ([Casper 2023][cas23] (p)); overoptimisation scales ([Gao 2022][gao22] (p)).
  • Reward hacking gets empirical ([Pan 2022][pan22]) and formal ([Skalse 2022][ska22] (p)) treatment.
  • Scheming analysed ([Carlsmith 2023][car23] (p)); control invented ([Greenblatt 2023][gre23] (p)); deception examples collected ([Park 2023][par23] (p)).
  • Evals become governance ([Shevlane 2023][she23] (p)); consensus risk statements ([Bengio 2023][ben23] (p)); catastrophic-risk overviews ([Hendrycks 2023][hen23] (p)).
  • Interpretability gets a sceptical survey ([Rauker 2022][rau22] (p)).
  • First "shallow review" index ([Leech 2023][lee23] (p)).

docs.title: 3.4 2024-2026 (17 papers)
docs.text:
• Papers: [Anwar 2024][anw24] (p), [Bereska 2024][ber24] (p), [Clymer 2024][cly24] (p), [Dalrymple 2024][dal24] (p), [Leech 2024][lee24] (p), [Phuong 2024][phu24] (p), [Slattery 2024][sla24], [Weng 2024][wen24] (p), [Bengio 2025 IASR][ben25] (p), [Bengio 2025 Scientist AI][bsc25] (p), [Hammond 2025][ham25] (p), [Korbak 2025][kor25] (p), [Lambert 2025][lam25] (p), [Leech 2025][lee25] (p), [Shah 2025][sha25] (p), [Sharkey 2025][shk25] (p), [Bengio 2026][ben26] IASR (p).
  • Operational turn: dangerous-capability evals on real models ([Phuong 2024][phu24] (p)), safety cases ([Clymer 2024][cly24] (p)), frontier frameworks ([IASR 2026][ben26] (p): twelve companies published or updated frameworks in 2025, per digest).
  • Control and monitoring become a second line ([Shah 2025][sha25] (p), [Korbak 2025][kor25] (p)).
  • Mech interp matures into reviews and open problems ([Bereska 2024][ber24] (p), [Sharkey 2025][shk25] (p)).
  • Reasoning models and RL return: "revenge of RL safety" ([Leech 2024][lee24] (p)).
  • Agents and multi-agent: [Hammond 2025][ham25] (p), [Bengio 2025 Scientist AI][bsc25] (p).
  • Governments author syntheses ([IASR 2025][ben25] (p), 2026 (p)).
  • Reviews grow: about 200 links (2023), about 300 (2024), about 800 (2025): [Leech 2025][lee25] (p).

docs.title: 3.5 Era claims to check
docs.text:
• 2014-2018 -> 2019-2021 shift from superintelligence arguments to ML-grounded failure modes: supported by titles; not tested.
  • Sharp rise of control and evals after 2022 is a count from this set; sampling bias is likely (the S list was built by the user).
  • No paper in the set from 2014-2018 treats LLMs [outside: LLM-scale RLHF began about 2022].

docs.title: 4. Influence signals (OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar, citation_counts.md)
docs.text:
• Highest: [Amodei 2016][amo16] (1412 / 3664), [Weidinger 2021][wei21] (492 / 1732), [Gao 2022][gao22] (63 / 1466), [Casper 2023][cas23] (105 / 1011), [Russell 2019][rus19] (775 / n/a), [Bostrom 2014][bos14] (1999, title-search match unchecked).
  • [Bengio 2023][ben23]: OpenAlex 356 vs Semantic Scholar 89; the two indices disagree strongly.
  • Blogs, books, living lists: no reliable count (Krakovna lists, [Weng 2024][wen24], Leech reviews, ELK).
  • Reading: practical/RL-and-LLM-methods papers (Amodei, Gao, Casper) lead on Semantic Scholar; theory and scheming papers (Carlsmith 7 / 103, Hubinger 57 / 344) are far lower. Hubinger's paper file says 142; the new table says 57.

docs.title: 5. Gaps in this analysis
docs.text:
• 43 of 51 papers are digest-only; any theme sentence marked (p) can change after raw reading.
  • Reception sections often say "no critique found"; absence of critique here does not mean none exists.
  • The 17 taxonomies are checked trees, but some node names in the S note differ (see disagreements.md section 6).

docs.title: Unified AI-safety taxonomy: master tree with sources on every node
docs.text:
A master tree of 12 areas and 70 sub-areas, built from 17 published taxonomies of AI risk. Every source node sits under the sub-area it maps to, quoted in the source's own words, so the tree shows where the schemes agree and where they differ.

Tags. Keys such as [omo08] ... [iasr26] are bibliography tags (section 7). A * after a node name marks a node taken from the author's notes rather than fetched from the source. (also 1.2) means the same source node maps to a second sub-area. X.0 lines hold nodes that apply to a whole area, not to one sub-area.

Names. Area and sub-area names (for example "3.1 Reward hacking, specification gaming, Goodhart") are synthesis, not the wording of any source. Quoted node names are the source's own. No node is listed unless it appears in a source; where the master mapping and a source differ on a name, the source's name is used and the difference is listed in section 6.

Name note (2026-11-23): the name of 11.2 was widened from "Safer design patterns, non-agentic AI" to cover designs that separate objectives (drives) from prediction and capability: a fixed or inspectable objective module (LeCun 2022), a goal-free predictor (Bengio et al. 2025), or an objective checked by an external verifier. Only [gdm25], [sr25] and [sg25] support the node; the added papers are listed in safety/drives_separation/. The ratings and justifications were made under the old name and were not re-run.

docs.title: How to read a line
docs.text:
- **3.2 Side effects, unintended consequences** — [amo16] "Avoiding Side Effects"; [dm18] "Avoiding side-effects"; [hu21] "4.4 Objective Proxies Can Lead to Unintended Consequences"

  • [sr25] "Black-box safety (understand and control current model behaviour)": the crosswalk mapping says "header, split below" and gives it no code. Placed in X here as a container; this is the only placement in this file not stated by the crosswalk.

  • [ji23] "RICE objectives (1.2.2)": one node in the source summary; the crosswalk mapping maps its four goals to four places (Robustness 4, Interpretability 8, Controllability 10.4, Ethicality 3.4). Listed in all four, counted once.
